ruling: D-242, Paul 2026-10-18: one Windows run is both A1 and A2 (the lighter standard of D-201); what a store records about the build itself is masked from this fixed, reviewed list instead of a measured A1/A2 variance
used_by: tools/compute_parity.py --single-reference (key/value tables of the SQLite stores only, per key and JSON field; both values must have the same JSON type or, for an entry with or_null, be that type or null, and look like their kind; the cells around a left-out field must be the writer's own text; shape differences, every unlisted key, every non-stamp row and every non-SQLite artifact stay exact; the file must be committed and clean, every needle must still be on its cited line in the tree built, and the report records the file's sha256 and HEAD blob)
never_listed: the bundle zip and its .sha256, density.json, the shown-areas table and manifest, the ingest/extend zips and every voter-derived row or column (compare_zip and compare_file never read this list); file hashes recorded in a store (roads_sha256, source_sha256: these stay equal only because the run judges both builds from one set of inputs); an absolute path; an id or a key
rules: store is the file name of a SQLite store a step of tools/build_step.py STEPS writes; table is its key/value table (metadata, or meta for the walk store); key is the exact key; pointer is '' (empty: the whole value) or a JSON pointer into the JSON value, `*` standing for exactly one segment (so `/timing/*` leaves out every timing but the set of phases must match); writer is path:line of the statement that writes the value; needle is a substring of that line (compute_parity refuses to run, and tools/test_compute.py fails, when the line no longer holds it, so an edited writer is re-reviewed); kind: clock = wall clock (an ISO-8601 time on both sides), duration = elapsed time and measured = a reading of the writing process (a number >= 0 on both sides); or_null: the value is this type, or null where the writer's call is unavailable; dumps: how the writer dumps the stored value (default = json.dumps(v), sorted = sort_keys, compact_sorted = separators (',', ':') and sort_keys), required for a pointer: both raw cells must equal their own re-dump, so spelling, spacing, escapes and key order beside a left-out field are compared exactly (a duplicate key or NaN/Infinity makes the cell plain text, which no pointer names)
